text:
Owen Power turns 24 today, and his season is the clearest step forward of his career. He's playing 25:13 a night, up from 21:39 last year, and has 17 points in 23 games, more than double last season's rate.

The interesting part is that the points aren't coming from the power play. He has none there, which Yahoo Sports pointed out as he closes in on a career milestone. Everything is coming at even strength, where Buffalo takes about 53% of the expected goals with him on and is better than when he sits.

If anything he's been unlucky. The Sabres have scored 7.7 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice. His own shooting runs hot, 11% against a typical 7%, so the goals may slow while the assists pick up.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at the 96th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists last season. He sets things up. What to watch: whether that on-ice luck flips during a hard stretch for a Sabres team trying to climb back into the race.
